title: Two Surfaces, One Test Boundary — Check

questions.prompt: From the browser's perspective, how many external surfaces does Agronomy Studio expose?
questions.explanation: The frontend talks only to the gateway (`/agronomy-api/*`) and the mock AI search; the domain services sit behind the gateway.
options: Two: the gateway and the mock AI search

questions.prompt: Limiting the number of surfaces the frontend depends on reduces the number of fakes and fixtures tests must manage.
questions.explanation: Each surface a client touches must be stood up or stubbed in tests, so a narrower surface means fewer fixtures and failure modes to reason about.

questions.prompt: Why can the gateway be tested without running the Blazor frontend?
questions.explanation: A stable, narrow contract lets each side be tested against the agreed URL shape and schema without the other side being live.
options: Because the frontend has no tests of its own
Because both sides share a stable contract that each can be verified against independently
Because Netlify runs the tests for you
Because the gateway has no logic worth testing
